title: OpenAI publishes first results for its Jalapeño inference chip
friendlyTitle: OpenAI shows early results for its own AI chip
summary: OpenAI says its first custom inference chip delivered higher throughput per watt and lower end-to-end latency than comparison systems across GPT-OSS 120B, DeepSeek R1, and Kimi K2.5 on the public InferenceX benchmark. The results are OpenAI’s own presentation and use matched user experience and package power ratings as key comparison points.
friendlySummary: OpenAI says its Jalapeño chip can answer faster and use power more efficiently on several large public models. These are early results published by OpenAI.
whyItMatters: Inference hardware determines how quickly agents respond and how much sustained AI use costs. A credible alternative to incumbent accelerators could improve capacity and pricing, although independent replication and production-scale evidence will matter more than launch benchmarks.
friendlyWhyItMatters: Better chips can make AI faster, cheaper, and easier to access. Independent tests are still needed.
